reason: Both reached the correct child-lock diagnosis and correctly stated no part was needed, but Conversation 1 got there more efficiently and without unsupported detours. Conversation 2 opened by misdescribing the symptom as 'no lights, no sound', then committed to a door-latch hypothesis and had the homeowner unplug and inspect the hooks before anyone asked about the display symbol, and its unlock instruction to 'unplug the unit first' then hold Stop is incoherent since the keypad cannot respond unplugged. Conversation 1 has its own flaws - it 'confirmed' the display was on before being told, and repeated a question verbatim after the customer said they would try it - but its questioning tracked the display and door sensibly and it never pushed a wrong hands-on fix. Conversation 2's closing prevention tip was a nice touch but not enough to offset the misdirection.
